verifier_note: Checked all 10 recipes' warrant sources by retrieval (WebFetch/gh api against doc.rust-lang.org, the rustup/cargo/rustc/clippy/edition-guide books, docs.rs at the pinned rapier3d-f64/parry3d-f64 versions, cargo-deny/cargo-vet/cargo-mutants/rust-fuzz books, and GitHub READMEs/PRs/issue comments/changelogs), cross-checked every engine_note against si-rpg-engine's main branch read-only via gh api (ci.yml, solver/build.mjs, solver/FLAGS.md, solver/src/lib.rs, solver/src/rapier_law.rs, solver/Cargo.toml, solver/Cargo.lock, solver/.cargo/config.toml, docs/dispatch-t3-platforms.md, docs/PHASE-2.md) and against the actual raw log of CI run 36121826863, and independently reproduced four load-bearing claims myself: the exact rustc rejection text for unstabilized trim-paths (three variants, byte-for-byte), the exact cargo-tree output for the wasm32 dependency graph (rapier3d-f64/parry3d-f64/simba/wide feature lists matched verbatim, plus the rayon-absent error), and the invalid_reference_casting lint firing on a direct &T-to-&mut-T cast but staying silent when the cast and dereference are split across two loops (compile_oracle.py, both PASS). Every one of the 61 warrant sources was reachable and dated 2021 or later. Two genuine defects surfaced: recipe 6 cites the wasm32-unknown-unknown platform-support page for '-Ctarget-feature=-foo disables a feature', but that page only documents the '+foo' enable form and target-cpu=mvp — the disable syntax is real and current, just documented on rustc/codegen-options/index.html instead; and recipe 7's engine_note places canon_zero in solver/src/lib.rs when the live repository shows it defined in solver/src/rapier_law.rs (js_min is correctly in lib.rs). The systemic weakness of this lane is exactly that kind of citation drift: individual numeric/version/API claims are exceptionally well-grounded (dozens of exact-string, line-number and CI-log matches, including exact byte counts and a rustc commit hash that verified against this rig's own toolchain), but a claim occasionally borrows the authority of a citation that supports an adjacent fact rather than the specific one asserted, or misattributes which file in a multi-file crate a function lives in — the kind of small slippage that only shows up by actually opening the cited page or the cited file rather than trusting the surrounding rigor.
